name: Tour

examples.title: Basic Tour
examples.code:
function example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const filtersRef = React.useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const exportRef = React.useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <Buttons>
        <Button ref={filtersRef}>Filters</Button>
        <Button ref={exportRef}>Export</Button>
        <Button color="primary" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
          Take the tour
        </Button>
      </Buttons>
      <Tour open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Tour.Step title="Welcome">
          A quick look around the list and its tools.
        </Tour.Step>
        <Tour.Step target={filtersRef} title="Filters">
          The Filters button narrows the list by status and owner.
        </Tour.Step>
        <Tour.Step target={exportRef} title="Export" position="left">
          The Export button downloads the rows you see as a CSV file.
        </Tour.Step>
      </Tour>
    </>
  );
}

accessibility:
There's no WAI-ARIA pattern for a tour, so each step is a
[dialog](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/), modal with the overlay and
non-modal without it:

- A step is a `role="dialog"`, named by its title through `aria-labelledby`, or by an `aria-label`
  on the `Tour.Step`, and described by its body. A development build warns about a step with
  neither a title nor a label.
- With the overlay, the step has `aria-modal="true"`, and the page under it is out of reach for
  everyone: everything else on the page is `inert`, the page doesn't scroll, the overlay takes
  every click, and Tab and Shift+Tab stay in the step. The target is out of reach too, so say in
  the step's body what it is: the spotlight tells a screen reader nothing.
- Without the overlay, nothing claims modality. The page and the target stay usable, by pointer
  and keyboard alike: Tab from Next moves focus to the target, to its first control or the target
  itself when it takes focus, and Shift+Tab goes where the browser sends it. Escape ends the tour
  while focus is in the step, so an Escape meant for a field on the page stays with it.
- Opening moves focus to Next, and ending the tour hands it back to whatever had it when the tour
  opened. On a step change, focus stays on the control used, so Enter on Next keeps going, and
  goes to Next when that control is gone, as Back is on the first step.
- After each step change, a polite `role="status"` line inside the step says where the tour is,
  "Step 2 of 5: Filters", since a dialog whose name changes isn't announced again.
- <kbd>ArrowRight</kbd> and <kbd>ArrowLeft</kbd> move between steps while focus is in the step,
  swapped under right-to-left text, but not from a text field, another control that uses the
  arrows, or a dialog inside the step. Nothing happens past either end.
- Skip and the close button always end the tour, so a modal step is never a keyboard trap, and
  <kbd>Escape</kbd> does too unless `closeOnEscape={false}`. A Modal or Dialog opened from a step
  takes Escape and Tab until it closes.
- The scroll to a target is the only motion: the spotlight and the step move with the target
  rather than glide after it, and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the scroll is instant.
- In forced colors, the overlay keeps dimming the page, since it's an SVG fill, the spotlight gets
  a `Highlight` outline, and the step keeps its border.

A tour sits at the modal layer, under toasts. Content inside a step that renders through a portal
of its own, such as a Popover with `appendToBody`, lands under the tour, so keep such content in
place inside the step.
summary: The `Tour` component walks a user through an interface one step at a time, each step a panel pointing at an element with the rest of the page dimmed around it. Each step is a dialog. With the overlay, the default, it's modal: the page under it is inert and still, Tab stays in the step and Escape ends the tour. Without it, the step is a non-modal dialog and the page stays usable.

props.name: children
props.description: `Tour.Step`s, in the order the tour visits them. Fragments are opened up, and anything that isn't a `Tour.Step`, a component that renders one included, is left out.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the tour is showing (controlled).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it shows from the start (uncontrolled). A tour has to measure its targets, so it shows from the commit after hydration, never in server markup.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with `false` when the tour ends: Skip, the close button, Escape, a click outside with `closeOnClickOutside`, or Done after `onFinish`.

props.name: value
props.description: The current step's index (controlled). One past either end shows the nearest step.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The step it starts on (uncontrolled), and goes back to each time it opens.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new index when Back, Next or an arrow key changes the step.

props.name: onFinish
props.description: Called when Done on the last step finishes the tour, before `onOpenChange(false)`. Skip, the close button, Escape and a click outside don't call it.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Dims the page and makes each step modal: `aria-modal`, the rest of the page inert and still, and Tab held in the step. With `false`, a step is a non-modal dialog, as a `Popover` is, and the page and its target stay usable, from the keyboard too: focus moves in and back, Tab from the step's last control, Next, goes on to the target (its first control, or the target itself when it takes focus), Shift+Tab goes where the browser sends it, and Escape ends the tour while focus is in the step. A `Tour.Step` can set its own, and a step that turns modal while focus is out on the page takes focus.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Ends the tour on Escape. With the overlay, from anywhere, while no overlay opened over it, such as a Modal opened from a step, is on top. Without it, only while focus is in the step, so an Escape meant for the page stays with the page. A popup inside the step, and content that calls `preventDefault()` on the key, take it first.

props.name: closeOnClickOutside
props.description: Ends the tour on a press outside the step, the overlay included. Content the step renders through a portal counts as inside.

props.name: portal
props.description: Where the tour renders: `true` for the `ConfigProvider` portal container or `<body>`, a selector or an element for another container, `false` for where it's written. Modal's shape, with a different default. The step and the overlay are fixed to the viewport wherever they render, so a `transform` on an ancestor of an in-place tour moves them with it.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: What every step's title renders as: a heading one level under the heading the tour's page sits beneath, or `p`.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words the tour writes.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the underlying element.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: One step of the tour: a title, a body and the element it points at. It renders nothing where it's written.

props.name: target
props.description: The element the step points at. Without one, or while it isn't on the page or has no box (in a closed Collapse or a hidden tab panel), the step is centered. A target that turns up later, or gets a box, is found then, and a development build warns once when a step shows without its target.

props.name: title
props.description: The title, which names the step's dialog. A step without one needs an `aria-label`, and a development build warns when it has neither.

props.name: children
props.description: The body, which describes the step's dialog. Say what the target is: a modal step leaves it out of reach, and the spotlight says nothing to a screen reader.

props.name: position
props.description: The side of the target the panel sits on. It flips to the opposite side when it doesn't fit, and stays inside the viewport.

props.name: overlay
props.description: This step's own `overlay`, in place of the tour's.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the underlying element.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props
